# Fixture provenance and stability

REQ-REPO-191 requires licensing and provenance to be documented for any fixture
that is not generated, and requires fixtures to stay stable once a golden or
reference test depends on one.

## Provenance

**Every fixture in this package is generated by code in this package.** There is
no recorded audio, no third-party sample, and no binary file of any kind.

That is deliberate rather than incidental. A generated signal has no licence to
track, no file to store in Git history, and no possibility of differing between
two machines. REQ-REPO-191 states the preference directly: deterministic
synthetic signals wherever they adequately test the required behaviour.

The pseudo-random generator behind `noise` is a counter-based mixing function
written for this package. It is not cryptographic and its output must never be
used for anything but test material.

## The measures of a cost

Two measures live here beside the fixtures. Neither is a fixture, and neither
generates anything.

- `relativeCost` in `processor-cost.ts` reads the processor time one workload
  takes against another, read in turn in blocks, and answers how many times the
  one costs the other. The tests of cost in the text, diagnostics and
  application packages hold code to it: a text against prose of the same length,
  or four times the work against the work. Every test of it is allowed
  `LONGEST_COST_TEST_MS`, 520 seconds, as its timeout, which the file derives
  from the measure's own cap and from `LONGEST_READING_US`, 12 seconds, the most
  one reading may cost, about twice the longest reading any proven defect makes.
  The measure enforces that: a reading that costs more fails the test when it
  ends, naming the side, so the bound holds of every measure answered, and an
  architecture rule holds every test of it to the timeout.
- `comparisonsIn` in `comparisons.ts` counts the comparisons of names a piece of
  work makes, at the collator, and stops the work with a failure once they pass
  a ceiling it is given. The tests of cost in the commands and workspace
  packages hold code to it: numbering a name beside four times as many names
  held costs at most `N_LOG_N_FOURFOLD`, 5.5, times the comparisons, the ceiling
  of the larger count.

They live here because the tests of the packages that share them may take this
package (ADR-0019): those of the text and diagnostics packages, whose own rules
leave it out of what they refuse, and those of every package no such rule
governs. The tests of the input and version packages may not take it, and the
domain package's cannot, since this package depends on it. They are test
tooling alone, as the fixtures are. They have no provenance to record: one reads
the machine it runs on and answers a ratio, and the other counts work, so a test
can hold a limit to either on any machine.

## What is deliberately absent

REQ-REPO-191 also names material that AudioGubbins will need and that this phase
cannot yet use:

| Material                                  | Why it is not here yet                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Openly licensed audio clips               | Nothing can decode a file until the codec system exists. A clip added now would be a fixture no test could read.                                    |
| Reference video clips                     | Sound-to-picture work arrives with the phase that owns it.                                                                                          |
| Example AudioGubbins projects             | The project file format is owned by the project and storage phase. The domain fixtures in `projects.ts` are the in-memory equivalent available now. |
| Example Godot project and event resources | Owned by the Godot integration phase.                                                                                                               |

When each arrives, its licence and source belong in this file, beside the
generated set.

## Stability

A generator here defines what every golden result taken from it means.

- **Do not change an existing generator.** Adding a new one is free; altering one
  silently invalidates every golden result that used it, and the tests will
  either fail for a reason nobody can trace or pass against a regenerated result
  that hides a defect.
- **Adding a parameter with a default is a change.** The default decides what the
  existing callers get.
- If a generator is genuinely wrong, the correction is a new generator with a new
  name, and the old one is removed only once nothing depends on it.

The only exception so far is recorded here for the record: the `noise` generator
was corrected on 2026-09-18, before any golden result existed, because its final
mixing step left every sample negative and outside full scale. The distribution
and amplitude tests found it.

## Naming

Every fixture carries a `name` built from its parameters, for example
`sine-440Hz` or `click-in-sine-440Hz-at-1000`. A golden result is filed under
that name, so the file says what produced it without anyone having to read the
test that wrote it. A test asserts that the names are distinct, because two
fixtures sharing a name would silently share a golden result.
